newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crudes at weekly high, talk thin.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crudes at weekly high, talk thin.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices reached their highest levels of the week Thursday, in reaction to stronger crude futures and flat discounts, traders said.

Outright prices for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude rose 30 cents to $18.40/18.50 a barrel in light discussion. The discount held at $1.05 a barrel under West Texas Intermediate, with BP, the grade's main producer, offering at $0.95 under.
Canada's IPL Energy Inc said its crude and products pipeline system resumed normal flows after a weekend shutdown that took out one millions bpd of the line's 1.4 million rate.
IPL said late Wednesday it would work with shippers to make up the lost throughput by the end of the month.

Texaco will take delivery of a 400,000 barrel South Blend cargo into Anacortes, Washington, to be loaded May 5 and delivered May 20, traders said. The refiner is trying to sell part of the cargo to another West Coast buyer.
A 2,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) shipment for California heavy grade in May sold at postings early this week, traders said.
